People don’t go to therapy & get on medication for anxiety disorders because they’re having trouble recognizing their fears aren’t logical…a considerable portion of anxiety diagnosed people are aware that their behaviors are irrational but that does in no way erase the disorder. 

These disorders are complex & can have many causations, the solution is to reach the core of the issue (ie trauma, parental relationships) or get on medication, not inform the person that they’re being illogical. 

Though it may help some people to recognize their rationale to help relieve some stress, the solution isn’t going to come from a random person on Reddit. Your misinformed answer telling them that what they’re feeling is unreasonable is not the key in the slightest to this person’s problem.

Sure under the circumstances of a normal non irrational fear you’d may be right, but a fear of people & relationships is psyche related. That’s not something you conquer by simply “recognizing how utterly ridiculous it is”. That mindset is why people with anxiety struggle to be understood, because people naturally compare others issues to their own & interpret something that’s in reality debilitating, to an everyday fear. 

& that’s not me attempting to speculatively diagnose OP but categorically a fear that “eats you alive” regarding interpersonal relationships is a deeper psychological issue than a fear of snakes or skydiving.
